# JRE #722 — Tony Hinchcliffe Recap

On November 16, 2015, Joe Rogan sat down with Tony Hinchcliffe, a multi-talented comedian, writer, and actor who had already made a significant mark on the comedy podcast landscape. This audio-only episode gave listeners an intimate conversation with one of the most distinctive voices in modern stand-up comedy.

Tony Hinchcliffe brought to the show the energy and comedic sensibility that made him a rising figure in comedy circles at the time. Best known for his work hosting the Kill Tony podcast alongside Redban, Hinchcliffe represented a new generation of comedians who were leveraging digital platforms to build audiences outside traditional comedy club circuits. Kill Tony had become a staple for comedy fans seeking sharp, irreverent roasting and banter, available to listeners through iTunes and the Deathsquad.tv network.

The conversation touched on Hinchcliffe's work across multiple entertainment mediums. As a comedian, he had developed a distinctive style rooted in quick wit and clever wordplay. His work as a writer demonstrated his ability to craft jokes with precision, while his acting credits showed his versatility beyond stand-up stages. However, it was the Kill Tony podcast that had truly captured the attention of comedy fans and cemented his reputation as a talented personality.

Kill Tony, the show Hinchcliffe co-hosted with Redban, represented a unique format in the comedy podcast space. The podcast featured roasting and comedic takedowns presented in a format that allowed comedians to showcase their improvisational skills and comedic chemistry. Available on iTunes and through Deathsquad.tv, Kill Tony had built a dedicated following among comedy enthusiasts who appreciated the show's unfiltered approach to humor and the genuine camaraderie between hosts and guests.

What made this JRE appearance significant was the opportunity for Hinchcliffe to discuss his journey in comedy and his work on multiple fronts. Though the full transcript of the episode was not available for detailed analysis, the conversation represented an important moment in documenting the rise of podcast-native comedy content. By 2015, podcasting had become an increasingly important platform for comedians to reach audiences directly, and Hinchcliffe was among the early adopters who recognized and capitalized on this shift.

The audio-only format of the episode didn't diminish the value of the conversation. For fans of comedy and podcasting, an appearance on the JRE provided valuable exposure and allowed Hinchcliffe to connect with Joe Rogan's substantial audience. The episode served as a snapshot of the comedy landscape in mid-November 2015, a time when podcasting was rapidly evolving as a medium for entertainment and when comedians like Hinchcliffe were helping to define what that medium could be.

This episode remains a document of Hinchcliffe's career during a formative period, capturing him as a comedian actively building his reputation through creative projects and media appearances. Whether discussing his comedy philosophy, his approach to writing jokes, or the mechanics of running Kill Tony, Hinchcliffe demonstrated why he had become a notable figure in comedy circles and why his work continued to resonate with comedy fans seeking authentic, unfiltered entertainment.
